newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GIGGS SET FOR PREMIER LEAGUE RETURN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIGGS SET FOR PREMIER LEAGUE RETURN.

text.p: Ryan Giggs will make his long-awaited Manchester United comeback against premier league runners-up Arsenal on Saturday in hopes of reviving his side's flagging fortunes.
Giggs has been plagued by a persistent calf injury which has led to him playing just 10 minutes of premier league football since September 29.

His previous appearance was as a late substitute during United's last league victory, a 1-0 home win over Liverpool on October 12, since when manager Alex Ferguson's side have lost four of their last five in the premier league and in Europe.
United are sixth in the league eight points adrift of leaders Newcastle.
Ferguson has pencilled Giggs in for Saturday's home game against Arsenal which should put him in line for the Champions League fixture with Juventus at Old Trafford four days later.
After coming through a reserve game on Saturday, Giggs said: "I'd love to play against Juventus, but we have Arsenal first and I want to get through that one before thinking about anything else.

"My calf felt a bit tight towards the end of the game on Saturday but hopefully it will be okay after a week's training. Being out for the last few weeks has been frustrating and I hope I can now do my bit to help us turn the corner."
Meanwhile, Ferguson has admitted the recent break in domestic football provided welcome relief from league pressures and could be the tonic his side need to revive their season.

He said: "To be honest because of the number of games we have played and the intensity of those games in recent weeks the internationals had to be seen as a break for us. That can bring a freshness to everyone."
